faq.title: Good to know
faq.q1: Does the other parent have to use eezzyflow too?
faq.a1: No. You can start perfectly well on your own. Invite the other parent when it suits you both.
faq.a2: The basics are free: calendar, messages and the costs that concern you. If you want more, you can take Plus or Family later. While the app is in its test phase, everything is open.
faq.q3: What does the other parent see?
faq.a3: Only what concerns your shared children: the calendar, your messages and the costs you share. They don't see your own calendar that you link.
faq.q4: Does it work if we live apart?
faq.a4: Yes, that's what it's made for. You set down the parenting schedule once and eezzyflow fills in the calendar automatically.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: Does my ex have to pay too?
faq.a1: No. Each of you chooses. If you pay for Plus, the other parent simply has the free basics, and the other way round.
faq.q2: What if the other parent doesn't want to take part?
faq.a2: Then you use the app on your own. The calendar and costs work for you, and you can always invite them later.
faq.q3: Can we take out one subscription together?
faq.a3: Yes, with Family. That works whether you live together or not: one subscription, and you both have everything. You agree between you who pays for it.
faq.a4: Via Settings → Account. You keep access until the end of your billing period.
faq.q5: Can the other parent use my Plus too?
faq.a5: No. What you share, such as the calendar, the children and the costs, you both see. The extra features only work for whoever has Plus or Family themselves.
